phases.title: Entry points
phases.description: Start with /pseo when a site already exists; it reads the project record and picks the next step. Start with the wireframe when there is only an idea.

phases.title: 01 · Direction
phases.description: Understand the site as it is, choose the first page family, and cluster what users are actually asking for.

phases.title: 02 · Data
phases.description: Decide where the facts come from, bring them in with boundaries, and model entities and relations before any page exists. The graph now exports the neighborhood view every page footer is built from.

phases.title: 03 · Pages
phases.description: Decide which pages deserve to exist, specify what each must show, prototype it with real records, then make it look designed. The IA footer is a required module.

phases.title: 04 · Integration
phases.description: Plug into the stack the site already runs on, implement the first family, and verify the real HTML.

phases.title: 05 · Release
phases.description: Define who drafts and who reviews, gate every page, and ship only with authorization and receipts.

phases.title: 06 · Learning
phases.description: Get a baseline, fix what is already live, and only then decide the next batch.

phases.title: PromptLab only
phases.description: Loaded only when the target is confirmed to be the PromptLab repository. The main table leaves these out on purpose.

skills.title: pseo
skills.description: Use it first: it reads docs/pseo/project.json, tells you which stage you're in, and picks the next skill.

skills.title: pseo-wireframe
skills.description: Use it when you only have an idea and want to walk, option by option, to a browsable wireframe of the whole site.

skills.title: pseo-site-audit
skills.description: Use it when you already have a website and want to know where PSEO should start.

skills.title: pseo-opportunity
skills.description: Use it when you have a few directions and need to pick the one page family worth validating first.

skills.title: pseo-intents
skills.description: Use it when you have keywords or customer questions and need to know which ones one page should answer.

skills.title: pseo-sources
skills.description: Use it when the direction is chosen but you don't know what data will keep the pages alive.

skills.title: pseo-ingest
skills.description: Use it when API, CSV, or web material has to become data you can check and re-run.

skills.title: pseo-graph
skills.description: Use it when you have a pile of material and need entities, attributes, and relations pages can reuse.

skills.title: pseo-page-plan
skills.description: Use it when data and user tasks exist and you need to decide which pages, navigation, and internal links deserve to exist.

skills.title: pseo-page-spec
skills.description: Use it when you know which pages to build and must define what each one has to show.

skills.title: pseo-prototype
skills.description: Use it when you want to see the page before development and check that it really completes the user's task.

skills.title: pseo-prototype-polish
skills.description: Use it when the prototype works but looks assembled, and you want it to look designed, or to compare a few directions.

skills.title: pseo-architecture
skills.description: Use it when the prototype is settled and you have to decide how data, templates, and publishing plug into the existing site.

skills.title: pseo-implement
skills.description: Use it when the spec is clear and you're wiring data and templates into real code.

skills.title: pseo-technical-seo
skills.description: Use it when the pages work but you need proof they're crawlable, URL-consistent, and free of index conflicts.

skills.title: pseo-content-workflow
skills.description: Use it when content will keep coming and you need to say who edits, who reviews, and where it publishes from.

skills.title: pseo-quality-gate
skills.description: Use it when you have candidate pages and want to know which can go to release review and which must be stopped.

skills.title: pseo-release
skills.description: Use it when the first batch has been reviewed and needs a safe, authorized release with real receipts.

skills.title: pseo-measure
skills.description: Use it when pages are live, or before that, to define how you'll judge whether they work.

skills.title: pseo-refresh
skills.description: Use it when pages are stale, slipping, or overlapping and you want to fix them before adding more.

skills.title: pseo-expand
skills.description: Use it when the first page family is proven and you're deciding what the next batch should be.

skills.title: pseo-content-create
skills.description: PromptLab only: draft a bounded CMS proposal for a Prompt or Article without touching the generated Git mirror.

skills.title: pseo-content-edit
skills.description: PromptLab only: prepare a revision-bound CMS proposal for an existing Prompt or Article.

skills.title: pseo-content-validate
skills.description: PromptLab only: validate a CMS proposal or mirror fixture; Git content is never the publication authority.

skills.title: pseo-content-pr
skills.description: PromptLab legacy name: prepare a human-review package; publication no longer uses per-item Git PRs.
